column2: the plan’s “when split buckets exist” wording invites key-presence logic, but committed per-step totals and `claude_sub` rows often carry `cache_create_5m=0` and `cache_create_1h=0` while `cache_create` is nonzero. summing only split buckets then yields effective create 0, collapsing ratios, excluding or mis-ranking real cache-write outliers (including zero-read `inf` cases on the claude subprocess lane).
scope requires documenting the new report in the run-log cli docs, but the plan only lists `docs/run-logs.md`. the command can ship without satisfying that acceptance item.

per-step ranking must reflect corpus-level create/read imbalance per `(skill, step, lane)`. averaging per-run ratios or ranking before aggregation can reorder outliers versus computing one ratio from summed effective create and summed read after grouping.

`report_tokens_scan.scan()` resolves the consumer repo via git, but sibling `measure_*` wrappers that write via `tokens._repo_root()` anchor on `__file__`. in a normal plugin install those roots diverge: scan reads consumer `larch-logs` while the tsv lands under the plugin checkout.

`runrecord` stores issue metadata and vendor totals but not skill; `report_tokens_scan._workflow` always returns `""`. the plan concatenates design and implement `scanresult.records` and groups per-step rows by `(skill, step, lane)`, yet helper signatures omit a `skill` argument and `measure_cache_efficiency()` only says to concatenate records. a flat merge loses which scan produced each record, so per-run `skill` cells can be blank or wrong and homonymous steps (e.g. design `3` vs implement `3`) fuse across skills. that corrupts `runs`, summed buckets, and outlier ranks in both tsv sections.

the plan sums raw `cache_create`, `cache_create_5m`, and `cache_create_1h` across runs in a `(skill, step, lane)` group, then applies `split_sum if split_sum > 0 else cache_create` on the grouped totals. committed reports can mix split-bucket rows and legacy combined-only `cache_create` rows for the same skill, step, and lane. once `split_sum > 0`, legacy combined-only create tokens from other runs in that group are discarded from the ratio numerator, so mixed-history groups are under-ranked.

committed reports store `per_step` entries as `{"step": "...", "totals": {...}}` (see `tokens._per_step_json` and `report_tokens_scan._phase_rows`). the plan points at `raw_report[lane]["per_step"]` but does not require drilling into `totals`. passing the row object into `_cache_lane_totals_from_mapping` yields zero cache fields and drops or mis-ranks every per-step outlier.
